headline: RBA LIFTS TO 18-YEAR HIGH — Fifth 2026 Hike Sends Australian Cash Rate to 4.85% in Split 6-3 Cup Day Decision
snippet: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its cash rate by 25bps to 4.85% on Melbourne Cup Day — its highest level since 2008 — in a split 6-3 board decision with three members voting to hold. The fifth hike of 2026 tightens borrowing costs for Australian-listed junior miners while a weaker AUD on rate expectations partially offsets the impact on gold and base metals revenues.

headline: WGC Q3 2026 GOLD DATA OUT — ETFs and Central Banks Hold Market Steady as Jewellery Demand Cools at Record Prices
snippet: The World Gold Council's Q3 2026 Gold Demand Trends report shows total demand holding steady, supported by continued ETF inflows and central bank purchasing even as jewellery buying weakens at elevated prices. The structural bid under gold remains intact despite the metal trading roughly 25% below its February 2026 record — key context for investors assessing whether the junior gold explorer re-rating has further to run.

headline: INDIA GOLD DEMAND HEADING FOR 6-YEAR LOW — Record Prices Shut Out World's Second-Biggest Consumer in 2026
snippet: India's 2026 gold demand is on track for its weakest year since 2020 as record-high local-currency prices have suppressed jewellery buying across the world's second-largest gold consuming nation. The WGC has also lowered its global gold investment demand outlook, citing slowing bar purchases that signal growing price sensitivity among retail buyers even in historically gold-hungry markets.

headline: I-80 GOLD GUIDES TO LOWER HALF — Nevada Ramp Trims 2026 Outlook as Archimedes Underground Targets Year-End First Production
snippet: i-80 Gold (NYSE: IAUX) revised 2026 production guidance to the lower half of its range after Q3 results, attributing the trim to a decision to leach Archimedes oxide material on-site rather than sell it — pushing some production recognition from Q4 2026 into Q1 2027. Archimedes underground remains on schedule to begin production mining before year-end, and the long-term hub-and-spoke target of 150,000–200,000 oz/yr by 2028 is unchanged.

headline: ASX MINERS CLOSE HIGHER AS OIL CRASHES 8% — Gold and Base Metal Stocks Lead November 3 Rebound, Healthcare Sold Off
snippet: Australia's S&P/ASX 200 closed higher on November 3 as crude oil fell roughly 8% on Iran peace-talk reports, lifting gold miners and base metals producers while energy stocks and healthcare names were sold. The session showed how the oil-crash-and-miners trade dominated even against the RBA's same-day rate hike to a 18-year high, with commodity equity positioning driving Australian index direction more than monetary policy.

headline: TSX GAINS 331 POINTS AS OIL CRASHES AND MINERS LEAD — Canada's Best Session in Two Weeks on Iran Peace Hopes
snippet: Canada's S&P/TSX Composite Index surged 331 points (+0.93%) on November 2 as crude oil fell sharply on reports of Iran's supreme leader backing preliminary peace talks, with materials and mining stocks leading the advance. It was the index's strongest session in two weeks, reversing recent losses tied to Iran war uncertainty; the gain was followed by a partial oil rebound on November 3 as peace-deal optimism faded.

headline: KAZAKHSTAN PLANS 150,000-TONNE URANIUM STOCKPILE BY 2050 — World's Largest Producer Signals Strategic Reserve Shift
snippet: Kazakhstan's Agency for Atomic Energy confirmed plans to build a 150,000-tonne strategic uranium reserve by 2050 to secure fuel for the country's planned domestic nuclear power expansion. As the world's largest uranium producer — roughly 45% of global mine output — Kazakhstan building a sovereign stockpile has direct supply implications for Western utilities and could amplify the tightness that has kept spot prices near $92–93/lb.

headline: MANHATTAN URANIUM WRAPS 24-HOLE MURMAC PROGRAM — 4,526 Metres Drilled, Six Holes Hit Anomalous Radioactivity Near Athabasca
snippet: Manhattan Uranium completed its 2026 summer drill program at the Murmac and Strike projects near Uranium City, Saskatchewan, with 24 holes for 4,526.4 metres total and anomalous radioactivity intersected in six Murmac drill holes. Assay results are pending for two Athabasca Basin-adjacent projects that sit on the eastern margin of the world's highest-grade uranium district, where active exploration and M&A has continued despite the broader mining sector selloff.

headline: URANIUM ONE OPENS FIRST PARAGUAY DRILL TARGET — 90,000 Ha Yuty Prometeo Breaks New Uranium Frontier
snippet: Uranium One launched its inaugural exploration program at the 90,000-hectare Yuty Prometeo–San José project in Paraguay after receiving a national prospection permit, marking one of the country's first modern uranium exploration campaigns. The reconnaissance-stage program targets sedimentary-hosted uranium in the Paraná Basin, using methods similar to those deployed at Uranium One's productive operations in Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan.

headline: 1911 GOLD HITS 14.86 G/T AU OVER 7.2M AT TRUE NORTH — Manitoba Infill Confirms Historic Vein Grades Ahead of Q4 Resource Update
snippet: 1911 Gold (TSXV: AUMB) reported 14.86 g/t gold over 7.20 metres from underground infill drilling at the True North gold project in Manitoba, with V-1020 Vein results in line with expectations while V-1010 returned below-target grades. The results feed into a Q4 2026 updated mineral resource estimate ahead of a forthcoming pre-feasibility study on this historic northern Manitoba gold system.
